title: Trump's Brennan Investigation Was Losing Its Lead Prosecutor Mid-Chase
description_short: Trump's Brennan Investigation Was Losing Its Lead Prosecutor Mid-Chase
description_medium: Maria Medetis Long had expressed doubts over case of John Brennan, whose agency said Russia boosted Trump in 2016. That is why this belongs in the catalog. A government that keeps turning institutions into revenge devices teaches everyone inside it what happens when they cross the boss.
description_long: The Guardian reported on April 17, 2026, that federal prosecutor Maria Medetis Long was no longer handling the investigation of former CIA director John Brennan after expressing reservations about the case. Long, a career attorney and chief of the national security division in the U.S. attorney’s office for the Southern District of Florida, told attorneys involved that she had left the matter, according to the report. The investigation concerned Brennan’s role in the intelligence community’s assessment that Russia interfered in the 2016 election to help Trump. The Justice Department did not immediately respond to the Guardian’s request for comment. The article did not report that Long had been fired, identify a replacement, or say whether the investigation was continuing unchanged. It also did not establish that Trump directed her departure or that the move was political retaliation. The report documents a prosecutor’s removal from a sensitive investigation and reported reservations, while leaving the reason and next steps unresolved.

title: Trump Cut Gun-Violence Prevention and Left Communities to Take the Hit
description_short: Trump Cut Gun-Violence Prevention and Left Communities to Take the Hit
description_medium: The Guardian reported that federal grant cuts under Trump led California gun-violence prevention nonprofits to scale back services. In Oakland, Youth Alive staff visit shooting survivors at Highland Hospital and connect them with support intended to deter retaliation. Prevention workers said funding losses threatened programs in underserved communities; the report did not establish that the cuts had caused a rise in shootings.
description_long: The Guardian reported on April 7, 2026, that the Trump administration had cut hundreds of millions of dollars from violence-prevention programs, including funding relied on by California nonprofits. Sergio Diaz of Oakland’s Youth Alive visits people recovering from gunshot wounds and helps connect them with services such as medical benefits and driver’s licenses to reduce the risk of retaliation. Youth Alive said 96% of the 118 people Diaz and colleagues served the previous year had not been injured again; that figure is the organization’s own reported outcome. The article also described Arise and Go, which had received $310,000 in federal funding through an initiative distributed by the Urban Peace Institute, to provide gang intervention, counseling, job training, and education connections in Harbor City and Torrance. Prevention workers said organizations were scaling back programs or laying off staff after the cuts. The reporting documents funding losses and concerns about service capacity, but does not show that those cuts caused a later increase in shootings.

title: Trump's Pope Obsession Looked Like a Very Old Grievance in Religious Drag
description_short: Trump's Pope Obsession Looked Like a Very Old Grievance in Religious Drag
description_medium: Manhattan church led by Norman Vincent Peale was known for opposing presidency of JFK – and Catholics in general. It fit the larger pattern of Trump treating spiritual language, religious authority, and public morality as arenas for grievance, ego, and old resentments rather than humility or reflection.
description_long: The Guardian’s April 18, 2026, report placed Donald Trump’s attacks on Pope Leo in the context of his early religious background. Trump attended services at Manhattan’s Marble Collegiate Church as a young man, and its pastor, Norman Vincent Peale, later officiated at Trump’s first wedding. When Trump was 14, Peale joined Protestant clergy who objected to John F. Kennedy’s presidential candidacy because Kennedy was Catholic. The report connected that history with Trump’s criticism of Pope Leo after the pope criticized the U.S. attack on Iran. This offers historical context for the religious figures around Trump, but it does not establish that Peale’s views caused Trump’s position or that a childhood grievance explains the current dispute. The title’s psychological and causal framing remains an interpretation. The article also recalls anti-Catholic arguments during John F. Kennedy’s 1960 campaign, placing Peale’s stance in a wider political setting. It supports reporting the historical association and current criticism while leaving motive unproven.

title: Trump: The UK's Foreign Office investigates Robert Maxwell & Russia
description_short: Trump: The UK's Foreign Office investigates Robert Maxwell & Russia
description_medium: After World War II, Robert Maxwell was transferred from the British Army to the Berlin headquarters of the United Kingdom’s Foreign Office, according to the linked timeline. It labels the event September 1, 1949, but its own account says the transfer and investigation occurred shortly after the war and that the exact date is unknown. It gives no investigation findings or Trump connection.
